stem: Jasper is a 2-year-old boy with asthma who presents to the emergency department with a viral prodrome, worsening cough and wheeze, fever (39°C), tachypnoea (RR 40/min), tachycardia (HR 150/min) and oxygen saturation of 90% on room air. He has reduced air entry and focal right lower zone crackles/bronchial breath sounds. Which one of the following is your first step in management?
explanation: In a child with acute wheeze/asthma and hypoxaemia, the first management priority is oxygen to correct low saturation while further treatment is initiated. Bronchodilator and steroid therapy can then follow, but airway/breathing support starts with oxygen.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: The item can be preserved: the correct first step among the existing options is supplemental oxygen because the child is hypoxaemic (SpO2 90% on room air).

optionExplanations.A: Useful for bronchospasm, but oxygen takes priority when saturation is low.
optionExplanations.B: Appropriate bronchodilator delivery, but not the first step when the child is hypoxaemic.
optionExplanations.C: Used for croup/anaphylaxis in selected situations, not first-line here.
optionExplanations.D: Important early adjunct in asthma, but not the immediate first step.
optionExplanations.E: Correct: hypoxaemia should be corrected first with supplemental oxygen.
